capabilities: Chat with a running Tomo container in a terminal tab
Stream active file, cursor position and selection to Claude Code over a localhost WebSocket
Execute Tomo instruction documents as batch vault edits with preview
Run optional .cjs hooks and write per-run log files
extras: Desktop only (isDesktopOnly: true); macOS is the verified platform, Linux experimental and Windows user-contributed. Detailed documentation lives in separate documents linked from the README. No telemetry or third-party services.
motivation: Tomo generates a lot of vault-shaped output and its review step is where you decide what to apply; the author wanted that apply step automated, with a preview and safe re-runs.
problem: Tomo's review output has to be applied to the vault by hand, and there is no way to talk to the agent or hand it live editor context from inside Obsidian.

relations.evidence: A live chat tab that attaches to a running MiYo Tomo (called Tomo further) Docker container
gives Claude Code in your Tomo container live ambient context

summary: Bridge to a local Tomo (Claude Code) Docker container: a chat tab, an editor-context WebSocket, and an executor for Tomo's instruction files.
